messages:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: Major incident detected — multi-region traffic-shift failing during DR exercise. Origin: us-east-1 -> us-west-2. High error rates and elevated latency for embedding and chat endpoints. Auto-fallback triggered but some requests are stuck in 'pending'. Paging oncall.
Maya: acked. I'm the primary oncall for infra. Looking now. What are the visible symptoms?
Sam: seeing BGP withdraws from a subset of us-east-1 egress routers to our peering. Some routes oscillating. Cloud provider status page shows partial control-plane errors in a single AZ in us-east-1.
Oncall-Eng: I'm on VPN to prov console, confirming API errors when updating route-weights. 503s from the provider API ~10% of calls.
Netbot: Automated check — cross-region latency spike between us-east-1 and us-west-2 for established sessions. Sampled TCP resets: 1.2k in last 5m.
Maya: TL;DR customers impacted? Any 5xx seen at edge?
Leo: Yes, 502/504 rates up on /v1/generate and /v1/embed. Errors tied to backend pool draining in us-east-1 where the ingress proxies are failing healthchecks.
Anya: I'm standing by for comms. Do we have an ETA to stop the shift? If shift is failing we should pause to avoid extended error window.
Sam: Trying to pause rollout — failing with provider API 503s. CLI output below:
```
$ cloudctl traffic-shift pause --region us-east-1 --id ts-2026-03-15-01
Error: 503 Service Unavailable: control plane temporarily degraded (request_id=abc123)
```
Maya: If control plane calls are flaky we should perform manual mitigations at the edge: 1) stop new traffic being routed to failing AZ, 2) scale up healthy proxies in us-west-2, 3) reduce DNS TTL where possible.
Oncall-Eng: Manual route action applied: set local route preference to prefer us-west-2 for affected prefixes. Command: ``routemgr set-preference --prefix 10.20.0.0/16 --preference 100 --region us-west-2``. Waiting for BGP convergence.
Netbot: BGP converging but a fraction of peers still flap. Exported peer state: ``flap_count > 5`` on two peers.
Sam: Cloud provider acknowledges partial control plane degradation in us-east-1 AZ-b. They've opened internal ticket CRT-4639. They recommend manual re-provisioning of affected egress instances.
Anya: Customer-impact note for CS: some customers may see increased latency/errors on embedding/chat for a subset of regions. Recommend status update to customers in NA/US East. Priya, can you draft?
CS - Priya: Drafting now. Will call out: "We are investigating increased errors/latency for requests routed through US East. Traffic is being shifted to US West; some requests may experience transient failures. No customer data exposure. Follow-up with ETA"
Maya: Oncall handoff incoming in 30m — if unresolved, please escalate to Eng SRE rotation. Also set incident severity to SEV2 -> possibly SEV1 if control plane degrades further.
Leo: Noted a strange symptom: KV cache warmup in us-west-2 showing >3s cold-starts for certain Llama shards causing increased tail latency while traffic pours in. Might need temporary cache pre-warm.
Oncall-Eng: Running prewarm script on us-west-2 proxies: ``for p in $(list-proxies --region us-west-2); do warm-cache --proxy $p --keys /opt/prewarm/critical_keys; done``
Netbot: Prewarm helped reduce tail to ~600ms from 3s for most proxies. Still seeing intermittent 502s for long-lived streams.
Sam: There's a stuck TCP connection state causing backend connection pool exhaustion on some proxy nodes in us-east-1; kernel shows many TIME_WAIT and orphaned sockets. Temporary kernel param tweak applied: ``sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout=30`` — helped free sockets faster.
Maya: Good. Continue manual mitigations. Also reduce DNS TTL where we can (edge TTL is 20s) to speed up client-side failover.
Anya: Comms update posted to status page and customers. Template includes affected regions, mitigation steps, and expected next update in 20m.
CS - Priya: Posted: "We are shifting traffic away from US East; some requests may see transient errors while we stabilize. Engineering working on mitigation. Next update in 20 minutes"
Incident Bot: Update: automatic incident timer — 20m elapsed. All hands: please post current action items and owner.
Maya: Action items: 1) Complete provider manual reprovision (Sam) 2) Continue route pref forcing and BGP stabilization (Sam/Netbot) 3) Prewarm caches & scale proxies in us-west-2 (Oncall-Eng/Leo) 4) Customer comms (Anya/Priya) 5) Monitor error budget and rollback plan ready (Maya).
Sam: Provider manual reprovision in progress. They say node replacement will take ~15-25m per host; doing parallel replacements.
Netbot: Observability note: majority of 5xx tied to a small set of proxy instance IDs: i-0a1b2c3d4e5f, i-0f9e8d7c6b5a. Marking them as quarantined in routing.
Oncall-Eng: Forced traffic shift retried with lower batch sizes; command: ``traffic-shift apply --batch-size 10% --region us-west-2``. Partial success: 60% of traffic shifted, remaining 40% hitting flaky us-east-1 egress.
Maya: If we can't complete the shift reliably, plan B is to route critical customers to dedicated endpoints in us-west-2 and leave non-critical onhold. Anyone for rapid routing change per-customer?
Anya: We can target top 10 customers with manual DNS overrides and loadbalancer IP mapping. CS to coordinate customer list.
CS - Priya: Sending list of top 10 affected customers now. Will include recommended mitigation steps per customer and contact windows.
Netbot: After route preference changes, errors dropped from 17% to 4% overall but some long-tail failures persist on streaming calls.
Sam: Provider reports their replacements completed for 80% of impacted hosts. Control plane now responding normally to our pause call. Pausing the global traffic-shift now to allow stabilizing:
```
$ cloudctl traffic-shift pause --id ts-2026-03-15-01
Success: traffic-shift paused, active traffic rerouted to stable pool.
```
Maya: Paused. Rolling back any aggressive route pref if it's causing instability. Confirming healthcheck success counts increasing.
Leo: Healthchecks passing across most proxies. Error rates holding around 2-3%. We should keep shift paused and monitor for 30m before resuming.
Anya: Customer comms update posted: "We paused automated traffic shift after partial failures; traffic currently routed to stable pools while we validate. Next update in 30 minutes."
Oncall-Eng: Handoff to next oncall (Sam) in 20m. Adding runbook note: if control plane flaps again, escalate to Cloud Provider SE.
Maya: Thanks team. I'll open the incident ticket for postmortem: INC-2026-0315-DR-01. Please add logs, timeline, and all commands used.
Incident Bot: Resolution summary (to be updated): initial cause: provider AZ control-plane degradation causing BGP/egress instability -> attempted automated traffic-shift encountered 503s from provider API -> manual routing mitigations + cache prewarm + kernel tweaks + host reprovisioning -> traffic-shift paused after 60% progress -> customer impact: elevated errors (peak 17%), some long-tail streaming failures, top customers targeted with manual fixes -> current status: stable at ~2-3% errors, no data exposure, monitoring.
Maya: Final check — leave incident open for a 4-hour observation window, schedule postmortem. If no regression, we'll close after that.
CS - Priya: I'll send proactive customer follow-up note with root-cause once PM has draft.
Anya: Assigning follow-up owners: Sam (networking root cause), Leo (runtime/prewarm tuning), Maya (traffic-shift orchestration), Anya/Priya (customer comms).
Sam: Acknowledged. I'll collect BGP dumps and provider ticket logs into the postmortem.
Maya: End of active updates. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
